newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Triplex pressurised to raise Cook bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Triplex pressurised to raise Cook bid.

text.p: British engineering group Triplex Lloyd Plc came under further pressure on Monday to raise its hostile bid for William Cook Plc after the steel firm reiterated that the current offer undervalued the company.
Analysts said Triplex would have to raise the offer price to at least 400 pence per share from its current 309 pence if it wanted to offer fair value to William Cook shareholders.
"The price has to be superior....around four pounds...," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
An offer price of at least 400 pence per share would value William Cook at more than 68 million pounds ($115 million), compared to the Triplex Lloyd offer which values it at 58.4 million pounds.
William Cook appealed to its shareholders on Monday to reject Triplex's offer saying the bid defied industrial logic.
It said Triplex Lloyd would not be able to effect any significant synergies or savings after the takeover.
William Cook is primarily involved in castings while Triplex Lloyd is a more diversified engineering group which serves the automotive and other industries.
Analysts backed Cook's observation saying there was very little synergy between the two firms.
"It is clearly the case where the bid is not about synergies. The argument can only be on what is complimentary..." said Guy Feld, an analyst at investment bank UBS.
Cook said it did not see any purchasing synergies either, with its primary raw material being steel scrap while Triplex's main raw materials are iron and ceramics.

However, Graham Lockyer, managing director of Triplex Lloyd said the firm believed a merger would cater to a larger customer base. "The basic technology, that is moulding, is still similar," he told Reuters.
Lockyear also ruled out any job cuts out of the 1,900-strong workforce of William Cook except nine full-time employees at its head office.

William Cook forecast its operating margins for second half to March 1997 would rise to 11.1 percent from 7.3 percent in the first half, mainly on lower refurbishment costs and a rise in sales at its George Blair defence products division.

John Caldwell, financial controller of William Cook, said on Monday that the company was still confident of maintaining its forecast of a pretax profit of not less than 10.7 million pounds against 8.47 million in the previous year.
"I will be astonished if they don't maintain the forecast," said Terry Smith of brokers Collins Stewart who recently met company officials.
A senior official involved with William Cook's defence said the company would like to "look at it" if the offer price was around four pounds per share.
"The quality of the offer would be important," the official said.
Triplex was forced to extend the offer to January 14 last week after it received only 5.83 percent of Cook's share capital by December 31, 1996.
